channel.title: The Daily Stack
channel.description: An automatically generated personal daily podcast in two parts. First, new AI product features from the major labs and the tools built on them: what shipped, how people use it, how you'd try it, and what informed commentators think, with a one-week-later follow-up. Then a lesson from an ongoing course on software development and AI: how software gets built, programming languages and their history, how LLMs work, agents and tools, and the real evidence on AI adoption and value. Each lesson ends with the thirty-second version you could use to explain it to someone else.
channel.itunes:subtitle: A daily class in software and AI, plus the new AI features worth knowing about.

item.title: Testing: how anyone knows the code works
item.description:
No feature news worth your time today. The lesson covers the three kinds of automated tests, the test pyramid, what coverage numbers do and do not tell you, and why verification is becoming the central job when AI writes the code.

item.title: The Mythical Man-Month: why adding people makes late projects later · plus: ChatGPT gets iCloud Mail and Calendar
item.description:
ChatGPT can now connect to iCloud Mail and iCloud Calendar on every plan, including free. And ChatGPT Pro users in the US can now text their always-on dot agent over iMessage or RCS. Then the lesson: Fred Brooks's law about late projects, his No Silver Bullet essay on essential versus accidental complexity, and how to use both to judge claims about AI coding.

item.title: Waterfall, Agile, DevOps: why the methods keep changing · plus: AI assistants and MCP come to Keynote, Pages and Numbers
item.description:
Apple is adding AI assistants to Keynote, Pages and Numbers for Creator Studio subscribers. On the Mac, it's also adding MCP support so outside agents can read and edit your documents. Both arrive in November. Then the lesson: what Waterfall, Agile and DevOps were each trying to fix, how a 1970 paper got misread, the DORA metrics, and why HealthCare.gov became the case study for government IT.

item.title: The software development lifecycle, and where the time really goes · plus: GPT-6.1 Terra and Siri memory
item.description:
OpenAI's new GPT-6.1 Terra is a faster, cheaper mid-tier model built for computer use and reading documents and drawings. iOS 27.2 gives Siri AI a memory of past conversations and more of your personal context to draw on. Then the lesson: the six stages of the software lifecycle, the evidence that maintenance and understanding existing code take most of the effort, and why that matters for judging AI coding claims.

item.title: What code actually is: from transistors to Python
item.description:
A quiet news day, so this episode is all lesson: the first of the course. We climb the layers of abstraction from transistors and machine code, through Kathleen Booth's assembly language, Grace Hopper's compiler and IBM's FORTRAN, up to Python, libraries and frameworks. We look at why every layer trades control for productivity, why abstractions leak, and what that means for the claim that English is the newest programming language.

item.title: Claude Duet, Anthropic's always-on agent; Gemini Notebook inside Gemini chat
item.description:
Anthropic opened a research preview of Claude Duet, a separate app where Claude watches your connected apps, sends a morning brief, and works on tasks in the background, asking first before it sends, pays or signs anything. Early reviews are split. Also: Google made Gemini Notebook a connected app, so you can work with your notebooks from inside an ordinary Gemini chat.
